title: Major Industrial Regions of the World

cards.h: Industry follows resources, then ports, then people
cards.b: Industrial regions are classic exam content: name the region, give its base and explain decline or growth. The old coal and steel belts have shrunk while East Asia has risen. Link to deindustrialisation and the rise of electronics clusters.

Alfred Weber (1909) held that firms choose sites with the least transport cost, then adjust for labour and agglomeration. Raw material, power, market, labour, capital, transport, government policy and agglomeration economies all matter. Footloose industries (electronics, software) can locate almost anywhere.

The Ruhr (Germany): coal, Rhine transport, steel, chemicals, built round Essen and Duisburg. Decline came after the 1960s; it has turned into services and culture. Others: Lorraine (France, iron ore), Saxony, Silesia (Poland), the Donbas (Ukraine), Midlands and Yorkshire (UK). The Rhine-Ruhr stays among Europe's densest.

The Great Lakes-St Lawrence belt: Pittsburgh (steel), Detroit (cars), Chicago and Cleveland. Based on Appalachian coal, Mesabi range iron ore (Minnesota), lake shipping. After the 1970s, decline made it the 'Rust Belt'. Growth moved to the 'Sun Belt' (California, Texas) and to Silicon Valley (high-tech).

Japan: the Pacific belt from Tokyo-Yokohama to Osaka-Kobe and Kitakyushu, built on imported resources and ports. China: eastern coast and Special Economic Zones (Shenzhen, 1980), Yangtze delta, Pearl River delta, Bohai Rim. Korea: Seoul-Busan. Taiwan: semiconductors (TSMC). The 'Asian Tigers' (Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan) used export-led growth.

Russia: Moscow-St Petersburg, Urals, Kuznetsk. Ukraine: Donetsk. India: Hooghly, Mumbai-Pune, Ahmedabad-Vadodara, Chennai-Bengaluru, Chotanagpur. Brazil: Sao Paulo. South Africa: Gauteng (Johannesburg). Australia: Sydney-Newcastle-Wollongong.

Alfred Marshall (1890) described industrial districts. Michael Porter (1990) argued that clusters raise productivity. Silicon Valley (Stanford, Palo Alto) grew round a university, venture capital and talent. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Shenzhen, Tsukuba and Hsinchu are other technopoles.

Offshoring cut manufacturing jobs in rich countries. Since 2018, trade wars, the pandemic and the chip shortage have encouraged reshoring and 'friend-shoring' (CHIPS Act 2022, USA). Supply chains move to Vietnam, India and Mexico, called the 'China Plus One' strategy. Critics say costs rise and gains are limited.

India's corridors: DMIC, Chennai-Bengaluru, Amritsar-Kolkata (the Eastern DFC base). Policy: Make in India (2014), PLI schemes (2020), PM MITRA parks, semiconductor mission (2021), and the National Industrial Corridor Development programme. Electronics clusters in Noida, Chennai (Sriperumbudur) and Hosur.

Likely questions: 'Causes of the decline of old industrial regions', 'Factors for location of the iron and steel industry worldwide', 'Why has Asia become the new factory floor?'

  • Map three regions per continent.
  • Use cause and effect: resources, market, policy.
  • Cite Weber and clusters for theory marks.
